ai-design-poster.png.what: Frame from the middle of the real run: the AI panel listing Finding where enzymes cut, Reading the method, Translating, the agent's reasoning about the His6 reading frame, a "Working · Checking its own design" line and Cutting with enzymes results (726 + 2656 bp, 44 + 2892 bp), beside the pUC19-GFPmut3b map.

notes: Plasmids shown: only the app's own pPL-* vectors and public pUC19-based clones that ship with it -- pPL-DEST (3,803 bp) in most shots; pPL-T7-His-GFPmut3b (3,618 bp, app/public/samples) in sequence.png and primers.png; pUC19-GFPmut3b + pPL-T7-His (expression_vector.gb) in ai-design.mp4 and app-agent.png; pPL-ENTR as a tab in ai-panel.png and app-window.png. No vendor plasmid (pcDNA-DEST53, pDONR221, pPS-*) appears in any frame.

ai_run is "real": ai-design.mp4, ai-design-poster.png and app-agent.png come from one actual Claude Code run through the app's agent bridge (23 steps, $1.267, about 2m26s from Send to done), recorded at deviceScaleFactor 2. The video is sped up 8x for the first 140 s and left at natural speed for the last 15 s. Nothing in it is staged.

The brief sent is the exercise's own text plus a new line "Write your answer in English." -- this machine's agent otherwise answers in Korean. That line is visible in the brief bubble early in ai-design.mp4; app-agent.png and ai-design-poster.png are scrolled so the bubble is out of view.
app-agent.png was picked from seven candidates taken every 10 s while the run was working; the others are in the capture scratchpad (hero2/).

New UI since the first capture: menu bar File / Edit / View / Sequence / Annotate / Clone / Analyze / Window / Help; view tabs Map / Sequence / Features / Primers / Cut Sites / History; map labels "Name 1,234" with +N isoschizomer badges; enzyme set "6 bp+ enzymes that cut once".
No dark mode: the app has no prefers-color-scheme styles, so there are no -dark variants. Everything is the light appearance.
Viewport 1440x900 throughout. PNGs are 2880x1800 (deviceScaleFactor 2) except ai-design-poster.png, walkthrough-poster.png and zoom-poster.png, which are 1440x900 frames of their mp4.
enzymes.png: the dialog does not span the whole window, so a sliver of the map (part of a label) shows at its right edge.
A zoomed circular map leaves part of the canvas empty by design, so frames in the middle of zoom.mp4 show white on one side.

Checked: no competitor product name (SnapGene, Benchling, Geneious, ApE), no vendor plasmid name and no 'PlasmidStudio' in any captured page text or frame. No Vite overlay or focus rings; scripted focus outlines were suppressed by stylesheet.
